staged_now.researcher_notes: No ENTSOG coverage in North Sinai (NO_NETWORK_MATCH; nearest nodes ~29-30 km).  A short industrial-to-industrial spur (~7-8 km straight-line) linking two separate cement clusters in the same central-North-Sinai heavy-industry belt south of El-Arish: the civilian Sinai Cement Company / Sinai White Cement complex at El Hassana, and the NSPO-owned ('military') El-Areesh Company for Cement plant at Jabal Lubna, further east/southeast toward El-Arish. Both sit off the same interior road network south of the El-Qantara-El-Arish corridor; no published map of the specific pipe route (vs. straight line) was found.  Same search process as P8052 (see that entry for the EGAS report / OSM / cement-cluster methodology). Additionally checked NSPO's own site (nspo.com.eg/nspo/cement.html) directly, which independently corroborates the 'military cement' identification and its Jabal Lubna / south-of-El-Arish location -- this is a genuinely independent, non-GEM primary source (the plant owner's own page), giving reasonably solid confidence in the END point identity specifically. Confidence tier: MEDIUM-HIGH on the identity of 'Military Cement' = NSPO's El-Areesh Company for Cement (owner's own site + OSM agree); MEDIUM on the Sinia Cement Industrial Area start point (same basis as P8052); LOW on the 16km/16in facts themselves (unverifiable in the cited source).  FLAG: length-plausible-but-high: straight-line distance between the Sinia Cement industrial area (El Hassana) and Military Cement (Jabal Lubna) is ~7.4 km vs. the sheet's stated 16 km -- a ratio of ~2.17x actual-length-to-straight-line. This is NOT the physically-impossible case (unlike P8052), but it is a wide margin for a short industrial spur between two nearby sites; flagging per the brief's guidance since it exceeds the ~1.4x comparison threshold. Plausible explanations: genuine road/terrain routing detour, or (less likely) one of the two industrial-area anchors is imprecise.
